subject: ggplot/reactive context error when subsetting data

messages.author: a3d24102116045c5
messages.subject: ggplot/reactive context error when subsetting data
parts:
I am a couple years new to R and brand new to shiny. I'm attempting to use a shiny input field to subset data which will then be plotted using ggplot and passed to the mainPanel. However, my code is throwing a "ggplot2 doesn't know how to deal with data of class reactive" error. However, when I remove the reactive() around the subsetting it throws the following: "Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive function.)" 

Is there something wrong with my code or approach here?

thanks.

Code:

server.r

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

SportPerf <- read.csv("F1213 Competitor Report - Combined - RatedAthletes.csv")
SportPerf$Year <- as.character(as.factor(SportPerf$Year))
SportPerf <- SportPerf[SportPerf$Decision %in% c("Admit/Matric", "Admit/Matric/Probation"), ]


shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  
  formulaText <- reactive({
    paste(input$sex, input$sport)
  })
  
  output$caption <- renderText ({
    formulaText()
  })
  
  SportPerf <- reactive({
    SportPerf[SportPerf$Sport.1 %in% input$sport, ]
  })
  SportPerf <- reactive({
    SportPerf[SportPerf$Sex %in% input$sex, ]
  })
  
  
  output$GPAplot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(SportPerf, aes(x=Year, y=Recalculated.GPA))+
      geom_violin()+
      stat_summary(fun.y=median, geom="point")+
      scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,4))+
      labs(x="Entry Term", y="Incoming GPA")+
      theme_bw()+
      ggtitle("2012 and 2013 Applicant GPAs by Team")
  })
    
  

})

ui.r

library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  
  headerPanel("Spread of GPAs by Team and Decision"),
  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("sport", "Variable:", 
                list("Basketball" = "Basketball", 
                     "Cross Country" = "Cross Country",
                     "Lacrosse" = "Lacrosse",
                     "Soccer" = "Soccer",
                     "Softball" = "Softball",
                     "Swimming & Diving" = "Swimming & Diving",
                     "Tennis" = "Tennis",
                     "Track" = "Track",
                     "Volleyball" = "Volleyball",
                     "Baseball" = "Baseball",
                     "Football" = "Football")),
    selectInput("sex", "Sex",
                list("Men's" = "M",
                     "Women's" = "F"))),
  
  mainPanel(
    h3(textOutput("caption")),
    plotOutput("GPAplot")
  )
))

messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: Re: ggplot/reactive context error when subsetting data
parts:
reactive(...) actually returns a function. You have defined SportPerf as a data.frame initially, but SportPerf <- reactive(...) will overwrite SportPerf as function. So I think the below is closer to what you want.

It's a good idea to replace the SportPerf <- parts of your program to the below. Hopefully this makes sense. SportPerf_sport_filter will filter the SportPerf data.frame, now SportPerf_sex_filter will use SportPerf_sports_filter(), which returns the filtered SportPerf, to further filter it. Then SportPerf_sex_filter() is passed to ggplot.

...
  SportPerf_sports_filter <- reactive({

SportPerf_sex_filter <- reactive({
    SportPerf1 <- SportPerf_sports_filter()
    SportPerf1[SportPerf1$Sex %in% input$sex, ]
  })
  
  output$GPAplot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(SportPerf_sex_filter(), aes(x=Year, y=Recalculated.GPA))+

geom_violin()+
      stat_summary(fun.y=median, geom="point")+
      scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,4))+
      labs(x="Entry Term", y="Incoming GPA")+
      theme_bw()+
      ggtitle("2012 and 2013 Applicant GPAs by Team")
  })
